“Brit(ish)” by @AfuaHirsch is a deeply personal work about her search for identity in a world in which her own country doesn’t properly regard her as one of its own. It’s a vivid, unsettling read, and forces reflection on all of us, especially white Brits. 😬 #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/zgZGVGTw4n

This is, not least, because racism can be found in all sorts of unexpected places. A striking similarity between all three books is that each one identifies disappointing heroines or heroes – admired figures who turn out to harbour racism. 🤨 #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/JosGW4CMY1

@RafiaZakaria notes Simone de Beauvoir as establishing strictly white criteria in defining “woman”, and @AfuaHirsch notes the (hidden) racism in the big philosophers she studied at university: Kant, Hume, Locke, etc. 🤦‍♂️ #StopRacism #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/mhZnQlWdRG
This prevailing attitude was no mere minor blemish, but caused a serious deficiency in the entire movement ⬇️🧐 #WhiteSupremacy #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/IPrlfJW31d

In her writing, Arendt in fact displayed a marked anti-Black racism, as charted recently by Kathryn Gines in her book “Hannah Arendt and the Negro Question”, which focuses on Arendt’s surprising opposition to desegregation of schools in 1950s America. 😳 #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/MOkn1j42pZ

She supports settler colonialism as a splendid manifestation of *action* (in the Aristotelian sense of “praxis”), calling it one of the “outstanding forms of achievement” of the European peoples. 🤔 #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/XVW22dLqCM

This is at the core of her outlook on life as a whole: one has to delve deep into her more rarefied work “The Human Condition”, but it is clear that she places people of colour at the lowest level of her “vita activa” hierarchy. 😧 #BlackLivesMatter

@RafiaZakaria raises the issue of FGM/FGC. A truly horrible practice which must certainly be ended, it has nonetheless become something of a tool for policing Black and Brown people. 🤨 #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/pZBcHuLGiA

Given that the UK and US governments are tackling FGM through police agencies rather than, say, the Department of Health & Human Services or equivalent, what does that suggest about their priorities? Policing of the Other, or their actual welfare? 🤔 #police #BlackLivesMatter

A very pertinent example here is the fact that Operation Limelight targets, among other countries, Yemen. This means that Yemeni travellers at Heathrow are routinely stopped and questioned about genitals. 😳 #police #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/kRLO11PSyL

Forgive me, therefore, for doubting that the US and UK governments have genuine concern for the health and wellbeing of Yemeni women and girls… #Yemen #HumanRights #BlackLivesMatter 🇾🇪 https://t.co/eMcLitxp9D
